waiting.$description: Light mode MCP input_required — paused for user input. Darkened from color.accent.warning's #d97706 (2026-08-20): AgentStatus renders this as text color (not a background fill), and #d97706 as text is only ~3.0-3.2:1 against light surfaces, failing WCAG AA's 4.5:1 for normal text. #af5100 holds ≥4.6:1 against every light surface token while staying in the same amber hue family.

elevated.$description: Light mode elevated surface — cards, popovers

active.$description: Light mode active step background tint

complete.$description: Light mode complete step background tint

waiting.$description: Light mode waiting step background tint

subtle.$description: Light mode low-contrast divider and border

muted.$description: Light mode de-emphasized or secondary text. Darkened from #6666aa (2026-08-20): the original was only 4.57:1 against color.surface.elevated, and defineAgenticTheme's neutralWarmth tint (lightness-preserving in OKLCH, but WCAG contrast is luminance-based, not OKLCH-lightness-based) could drop it below the 4.5:1 AA floor. 5.3:1 baseline leaves headroom for the tint.

accent.$description: Text on accent backgrounds. Light mode's interactive/danger/success accents are dark enough for white text to pass WCAG AA; color.accent.warning is a lighter amber and uses color.text.on.warning instead — see its description

danger.$description: Text on the danger background. Fixed independently of color.text.on.accent (see dark-mode counterpart) — light mode's deep danger red passes with white text at ≈4.8:1

warning.$description: Text on the warning background. White fails here (light mode's amber warning is too light — ≈3.2:1, below AA's 4.5:1 for normal text); near-black holds ≈6.2:1

success.$description: Light mode success and done state

warning.$description: Light mode warning and waiting state

danger.$description: Light mode error and danger state
